en: The Philippines has 7,641 islands, a count updated from the old 7,107 figure by NAMRIA in 2016.
Mount Apo in Davao is the highest Philippine mountain at 2,954 meters, not Mount Pulag as many believe.
Laguna de Bay in Luzon is the largest lake in the Philippines, not Lake Lanao in Mindanao.
Taal Volcano sits on an island inside Taal Lake on Luzon, forming a volcano within a lake within an island.
The Cagayan River in northeastern Luzon is the longest river in the Philippines at approximately 505 kilometers.
Davao City is the largest city in the Philippines by land area at 2,444 square kilometers, not Manila.
Mayon Volcano in Albay is renowned for its nearly perfect symmetrical cone shape, not a flat or irregular summit.
Luzon is the largest island group in the Philippines, covering about 109,965 square kilometers, not the smallest.
Baguio City has cool weather because of its high elevation of roughly 1,500 meters, not its distance from the equator.
The Philippines is divided into three main island groups—Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao—not just two as some think.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park is located in the Sulu Sea, not in the West Philippine Sea.
Mount Pulag in Benguet is the second-highest mountain in the Philippines at 2,928 meters, not the highest peak.
